notes: Gilead paid $4.9B for Forty Seven's magrolimab — an anti-CD47 (don't-eat-me-signal blocker) monoclonal antibody. Phase 2 at deal time in MDS, AML, and other hematologic malignancies; later expanded to solid tumors. CRITICAL POST-DEAL CONTEXT: Magrolimab failed pivotal AML and MDS Phase 3 trials in 2023-2024; Gilead discontinued the program in Feb 2024. The $2B peak sales estimate is the pre-failure consensus; post-failure realistic peak is near zero. Include in the cohort because the deal terms are real and acquirers DO pay for Phase 2 oncology mAbs with novel mechanisms — including ones that subsequently fail. This is the framework working as intended: M&A premia on Phase 2 oncology mAbs reflect real risk.
selection_rationale: Recent (2020), single-asset, oncology mAb M&A at Phase 2 — important benchmark for the multiple paid for pre-pivotal oncology biologics with novel mechanisms. The post-deal failure is a feature, not a bug: the cohort should reflect what acquirers actually pay, including the deals that didn't work out.
source: Gilead press release Mar 2 2020; Forty Seven SEC filings; Gilead Q4 2023 + Q1 2024 earnings (magrolimab discontinuation disclosure).
